verdict.root_cause: An automated resource_limits change at 15:11:51Z lowered the ad container's memory limit to 144m [tr_0fded08a4b2e]. Under that ceiling the ad process cannot stay resident: ad's logs show normal serving at 14:24 and then at least eight distinct JVM startup sequences between ~15:31 and 15:35:53, several reaching the application's own 'service starting' line before dying again — a crashloop, not one restart [tr_ba0e1637b35c]. The kill comes from outside the runtime, which is why no OutOfMemoryError token appears in ad's logs [tr_9b573018eac2] and why ad's error ratio stays under 1% while 29 of 96 intervals are undefined — ad served no traffic at all in those intervals because the process was down [tr_c6dda981caac, tr_650bcbff6bc2]. When ad is up it is healthy: no error spans, GetAds in 0.3–4.7ms, no outbound calls [tr_613998684b05]. The intermittent bursty error profile at frontend-proxy (mean ~2.8%, peaks ~11%, floor 0) is what a dependency that keeps vanishing and returning produces [tr_4d991b3199ae]. The mechanism is memory exhaustion against a lowered limit; the fix is restoring the prior limit, since a restart returns the container under the same ceiling.
verdict.reasoning: The only change in ad's window is a memory ceiling lowered minutes before onset, with no deploy, image, env or flag mutation recorded [tr_0fded08a4b2e], which forecloses bad_deploy and config-edit explanations. ad's own log shows a repeating boot loop reaching application init [tr_ba0e1637b35c], excluding process_freeze (a frozen process writes nothing) and an image that never boots. The missing OOM token [tr_9b573018eac2] is consistent with a container-level kill rather than an in-JVM heap error, and the NOP-logger warnings mean app-level error lines would be suppressed anyway. Metrics show absence rather than failure: sub-1% errors where ad reports, and a third of intervals with no traffic at all [tr_c6dda981caac, tr_650bcbff6bc2] — a crashing service goes undefined, a failing one goes toward 1. Traces show ad fast and dependency-free whenever alive [tr_613998684b05], ruling out dependency_latency inside ad. The edit is how it started; exhaustion against the limit is what is happening, so revert_config, not restart, removes it.
open_questions: No memory working-set, restart-count or OOMKilled exit-code series was ever retrieved [tr_650bcbff6bc2]; the kill is inferred from the restart loop plus the limit change, not directly observed, and the prior limit value is unrecorded.
frontend-proxy alerted at 15:15:46, ~16 minutes before the first visible ad restart cycle; no per-timestamp series exists for the proxy [tr_4d991b3199ae], so the earliest errors are unattributed.
Eight edges and nine other services were never measured; whether ad alone accounts for the full blast radius is untested, and flagd's change log was only queried forward from onset [tr_aad7a8e78bb5].

alternatives.root_cause: The proxy's error bursts originate in an unexamined service and ad's restart loop is secondary or coincident.
alternatives.why_not: No positive evidence supports it, while the ad path has a change record, a crashloop and traffic gaps that interlock; the proxy's zero-floor bursty profile matches a dependency repeatedly vanishing.

alternatives.root_cause: A flag flipped before the queried window broke a flagged code path, leaving no change record.
alternatives.why_not: A flag failure shows fast errors with span statuses naming the flag; ad's traces carry no error spans [tr_613998684b05] and its logs no flag-evaluation lines [tr_ba0e1637b35c], and a flag flip does not restart a JVM eight times.

proposal.expected_effect: Restoring ad's declared container configuration (removing the 144m memory ceiling applied at 15:11:51Z) should end the crashloop. Observable as: (1) in Loki, {service="ad"} stops producing repeated JVM startup banners (JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS / CDS / otel-javaagent-version / 'service starting') — after the recreate there should be exactly one startup sequence and then steady AdService request lines, not eight in four minutes; (2) in Prometheus, ad's span-metrics call-rate series becomes continuously defined — the undefined intervals that made 29 of 96 samples blank should stop appearing, because the process stays resident and keeps serving; (3) frontend-proxy's error ratio should settle at its floor of 0 instead of bursting to ~11%, since the bursts are hypothesised to be ad vanishing and returning.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if, more than ~3 minutes after the recreate, Loki still shows repeated JVM startup banners for ad (a second crashloop under the restored config), or if ad stays up cleanly but frontend-proxy's error ratio continues to burst above ~5%. The second outcome is the more likely miss: frontend-proxy alerted at 15:15:46, roughly 16 minutes before the first visible ad restart cycle, and no per-timestamp proxy series exists [tr_4d991b3199ae], so the earliest proxy errors are unattributed and may have a separate cause. Also note what cannot be observed: the OOM-kill itself was never measured — no working-set, restart-count or OOMKilled exit-code series was retrieved [tr_650bcbff6bc2] and no OutOfMemory token appears in ad's logs [tr_9b573018eac2] — so success here is inferred from the restart loop stopping, not from watching memory fall below a limit. If the loop stops, that is consistent with the diagnosis but does not prove the kill was memory-driven.
proposal.risk: Three concrete risks. (1) The prior memory limit is unrecorded (null before-state in the change log), so this restores the service's declared definition rather than a known-good measured value; if the declared definition carries no limit, ad runs unbounded and a genuine leak — which the automated rightsizing may have been reacting to — would then pressure the host and its co-located containers instead of being contained to ad. (2) The revert recreates the container, so ad's in-process cache is discarded and callers see a connection reset for the duration; if ad was in fact healthy between restarts (traces show clean sub-5ms GetAds [tr_613998684b05]), this adds a fresh outage to a service that was partly working. (3) If the real driver of the frontend-proxy errors is upstream of ad or in an unmeasured edge — eight edges and nine services were never measured — this consumes an approval, resets ad, and leaves the actual fault running while appearing to have acted.
proposal.blast_radius: ad itself, for the length of the recreate. Directly: frontend, which calls ad and will see resets/failed GetAds during the recreate; frontend-proxy and load-generator see that propagate as a brief error burst on the user_get_ads path. Downstream: flagd is reached from ad, so it sees ad's flag-evaluation traffic stop and then resume. No other service's configuration is touched, and the reverted value is a resource limit rather than a dependency address, so no traffic moves between services.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical multi-service alerting spanning proxy, frontend and ad over a ~19 minute spread, with no open incident to attribute it to. Fan-in at the frontend with an ad/flagd branch is consistent with several mechanisms, so the fault class is best left open for evidence.
